facts_of_case: The parties were in a marital dispute. The wife claimed alimony pendente lite and the trial court awarded maintenance of Rs.5,000/- per month. The husband appealed.

legal_principles.principle: Where in any proceeding under the Hindu Marriage Act, it appears to the Court that either the wife or the husband has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may order maintenance.
legal_principles.held: Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 clearly provides that where in any proceeding under this Act it appears to the Court that either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may, on the application of the wife or the husband, order the

legal_principles.principle: The Court should not have awarded maintenance to the wife if the husband has instituted a suit for restitution of conjugal right under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: I am not at all impressed by the aforesaid submission.

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the maintenance award would stand.
